id: title:Gilbert09:stop retrying an expired instance certificate

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a descriptive error message and classification for Matomo certificate-expiry failures, potentially improving user diagnostics and preventing unnecessary retry loops.
review.reason: The change adds a backend error classification entry and a corresponding test assertion. This does not implement the certificate-expiry detection or modify the HTTP client, but it establishes a clear, permanent failure classification and user-facing error message for this specific warehouse ingestion error. This is a localized maintenance and documentation improvement.
review.uncertainty: The score relies on the assumption that adding the classification and message is sufficient for tier 1, while the actual implementation of the detection and retry prevention is absent. No tier 2 or 3 evidence exists.

observations.limitations: Only backend error classification and a corresponding test assertion are supplied. No implementation of the actual certificate-expiry detection, no change to the HTTP client or retry configuration, and no change to the warehouse connector or warehouse-side behavior. The score cannot be assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new key-value pair to the non-retryable error classification dictionary, treating the Matomo certificate-expiry error as a permanent failure rather than a retryable one.
observations.code_quote: "certificate has expired": "PostHog could not connect to your Matomo instance because its SSL certificate has expired. Renew the certificate on your Matomo host, then try again.",
observations.posthog_connection: This could prevent PostHog from repeatedly retrying warehouse ingestion requests against a Matomo host whose SSL certificate has expired, potentially avoiding unnecessary request storms and allowing the warehouse ingestion workflow to fail fast and surface a clearer error to the user.
